title: Use a choropleth to show a rate on the shapes of the states, in a few classes a margin of error cannot blur.
rule: A choropleth shades each place by its class, a range of values that share one shade. Shade each state in four classes at most on the sequential steps (Rule 14.5), the step nearest the page color with a 1 px edge, and draw the borders as thin lines of the page color. Set the classes and their note by Rule 14.9’s test for a class map, and print each state’s code on its shape or beside it (Rule 14.3). Draw the District of Columbia as a small square beside Maryland, set Alaska and Hawaii apart in thin frames, and put the national figure above the map (Rule 14.6). On a phone, where outlines leave most codes no room, draw a tile grid map, one square a state (Rule 14.114), in the same classes, each code on its square (Rule 14.12).
use_when: The reader asks where a rate runs high or low across the states, and the shape of the country helps them find their own.

use_instead.when: Each state counts once, whatever its size
Size matters as much as the rate
The reader looks up one state’s exact figure

text: A reader finds a state by its shape faster than by a list, and a few classes turn the rates into a pattern at a glance. Classes wider than the survey’s margins keep a state’s shade within one class of what the survey can tell.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form choropleth: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s78; encode code, value and margin; labels.bins sets where each class starts, labels.class_labels its words, labels.nation and nation_label the national figure, labels.dc the District of Columbia’s square; the boundary file is the spec’s second dataset.
